# Assembly Companion – public API

<!-- Generated by tools/api_doc.py from api.describe(): edit the docstrings
     in freecad/assembly_companion/api.py, then run the tool. -->

`freecad/assembly_companion/api.py` is the stable entry point for scripts,
macros and other addons (a third-party MCP addon may call it too). It is
headless-safe (no dialog, no active
view), takes the document explicitly (object, internal name or label),
objects by internal name and files by path, and returns plain data accepted
by `json.dumps`. Functions that change a document accept `dry_run=True`.
Errors are the typed exceptions of `errors.py` (`AssemblyCompanionError`
and its subclasses `NoDocumentError`, `NoAssemblyError`,
`ObjectNotFoundError`, `UnsupportedObjectError`, `SourceNotFoundError`,
`GuiRequiredError`); each has `to_dict()`.

```python
from freecad.assembly_companion import api
api.describe()                    # this catalogue, as data
api.bom("Assembly")               # document by name, label or object
```

API version: **1** (incremented at every breaking change).

## Functions

### `describe()`

Catalogue of the public functions: name, docstring, parameters with
their defaults, for a script to discover the API on its own.

### `list_components(doc)`

Components of the assemblies of `doc` (Links and parts directly in an
assembly): name, label, state (frozen / linked / local / lightweight /
broken), source file, joints using them.

### `freeze_parts(doc, names=None, dry_run=False, mode='structure')`

Freeze the Links and sub-assemblies `names` (internal names; None =
every external one): each one points to a dead BREP copy stored in the
document. Containers (Std_Part, STEP import groups) and sub-assemblies
are frozen with their parts, names, placements and joints (mode
"structure"), or as ONE solid per Link (mode "block"). A Link whose
content cannot be frozen is left linked and listed in "skipped"; one
undo step, nothing changed when an error occurs.
-> {"frozen": [...], "skipped": [{"name", "reason"}], "refs_updated": n}

### `relink_parts(doc, names=None, dry_run=False)`

Point frozen Links back to their source file (None = all of them).
-> {"relinked": [...], "missing_source": [{"name", "file"}]}

### `delete_part_joints(doc, names, dry_run=False)`

Delete every joint and grounding of the components `names`.
-> {"deleted": [joint names]}

### `diagnose(doc)`

Check every joint reference and the frozen copies, without changing
the document. -> {"references": [...], "broken": n, "ok": n,
"copies": [{"name", "topo_history"}], "unused_copies": [...]}

### `outdated_parts(doc)`

Frozen parts and the state of their source file.
-> [{"name", "label", "state": "outdated"|"ok"|"missing", "source_file",
"frozen", "source_saved"}]

### `refreeze_outdated(doc, names=None, dry_run=False)`

Refreeze the frozen copies `names` (None = every outdated one) from
their saved source file. -> {"refrozen": [...]}

### `bom(doc, hierarchical=False)`

Bill of materials of `doc`, frozen parts under their original name.
Flat: [{"quantity", "part", "source_file", "state"}] sorted by part, the
parts of sub-assemblies counted in. hierarchical=True: sub-assemblies
are rows of their own with their parts in "children" (same keys,
recursively).

### `export_bom_csv(doc, path, hierarchical=False)`

Write the bill of materials of `doc` to the CSV file `path` (with a
"Level" column when hierarchical). -> {"path", "rows"}

### `check_collisions(doc, skip_fasteners=True, show=False)`

Pairs of parts whose solids overlap. `show` adds the red "Collisions"
object to the document. -> {"parts": n, "pairs": [{"a", "b", "volume"}]}

### `archive(doc, path, include_frozen_sources=False)`

Zip `doc` with every file it needs (and optionally the source files of
its frozen parts). -> {"path", "files": [names in the zip], "missing": [...]}

### `replace_component(doc, name, path, object_name=None, all_instances=False, dry_run=False)`

Point the component `name` (and with all_instances the other Links using
the same part) to `object_name` of the file `path` (default: the same
internal name as now), joints kept; frozen components are frozen again.
-> {"replaced": [...], "refrozen": [...], "object": name, "file": path}

### `duplicate_components(doc, names, with_joints=False)`

Clone the components `names` in their assembly (same target, place and
colours), with their joints when `with_joints`.
-> {"clones": [{"source", "clone"}], "joints": [new joint names]}

### `make_lightweight(doc, names=None, dry_run=False)`

Replace the components `names` (None = every component of the
assemblies) by lightweight ones: skeleton + mesh skins, joints kept.
-> {"lightweight": [Link names], "containers": [names]}

### `restore_full(doc, names=None, dry_run=False)`

Put lightweight components back to their source parts, joints included;
frozen ones are frozen again. -> {"restored": [...], "refrozen": [...]}

### `new_part_from_selection(doc, selection, path, label=None, linked=False, insert=True)`

Create the part file `path` holding a Body with a SubShapeBinder of the
`selection` = [[root object name, subname], ...] (e.g.
[["Assembly", "Plate.Face6"]]). Default: independent copy (detached
binder), inserted into the assembly at its place. `linked`: binder that
follows the assembly (not inserted: the files would depend on each other).
-> {"path", "document", "body", "binder", "inserted": Link name or None}

### `selection_sets(doc)`

Selection sets stored in `doc`. -> [{"name", "label", "members": [...]}]
A member is "RootName|sub.path." (object) or "RootName|sub.path.Face6".

### `create_selection_set(doc, label, members)`

Store a new selection set. -> {"name", "label", "members"}

### `selection_set_members(doc, name, expand=False)`

Members of the set `name`; `expand` lists individual parts (element
members kept as they are). -> [member keys]

### `combine_selection_sets(doc, a, b, op, label=None)`

New set from the sets `a` and `b`: op = "union" | "intersection" |
"difference" (on individual parts). -> {"name", "label", "members"}

### `group_fasteners(doc, names=None)`

Move fasteners of the Fasteners workbench into the Std_Part of their
body (None = all). -> {"moved": [...], "parts_created": [...], "skipped": [...]}

### `reactivate_assembly(doc)`

GUI only: clear a stuck task panel / edit / active object and activate
the assembly again. -> {"active": bool}

### `scan_library(folder=None, recursive=True)`

Read the parts library on disk (default: the "Parts library" folder of
the preferences), or only `folder` when recursive=False. The explorer
disk cache of the library is updated with the result.
-> {"folder", "count", "folders": [{"folder", "files": [{"path", "name",
"mtime", "size"}]}]}

### `list_library(folder=None)`

Parts library as last seen by the explorer (disk cache, no folder
walk: instant on a network share); scans it when there is no cache.
Same return value as scan_library().

### `import_step(doc, step_path, assembly=None, mode='file', file_path=None, insert=True)`

Import the STEP file `step_path` as one Std_Part (import groups turned
into Parts: every element visible and usable for joints) and insert it
into `assembly` (name; None = the first assembly of `doc`). mode "file":
the Part is saved in a new .FCStd (`file_path`, default next to the
assembly, named after the STEP file; never overwritten) and linked;
mode "document": the Part is created in `doc` as a component.
-> {"mode", "file", "part", "document", "inserted", "solids"}

### `extract_bodies(doc, names, folder=None, prefix=None, revision=None, replace=False, dry_run=False)`

Copy each PartDesign Body `names` with its whole tree (sketches,
features, datums, spreadsheets its expressions use) into its own new
file PREFIX_NNNr_<label>.FCStd in `folder` (defaults: the new-part
preferences, folder of `doc`). Binders become detached, outside
attachments deactivated: the new files stand alone. replace=True puts a
Link to each new part in place of the body (joints kept), one undo step.
-> {"bodies": [{"body", "file", "copied", "standalone", "external",
"volume", "faces", "new_volume", "new_faces"}], "replaced": [...]}

### `new_file(path, part=None, body=None)`

Create and save the new part file `path` (never overwritten): an
App::Part labelled `part` (None: no container) holding an empty
PartDesign Body labelled `body` (None: no Body; at the root without a
container). The document stays open.
-> {"path", "document", "part", "body"}

### `analyze_dependencies(doc)`

Documents `doc` depends on (directly or through another file) and why
FreeCAD may ask to save them with it. -> [{"document", "label", "file",
"open_in_tab", "partial", "modified", "touched": [labels], "used_by":
[object names of doc], "via": label of the linking document}] (modified
first)

### `save_dependencies(doc, names=None)`

Save the dependencies `names` of `doc` (None = every modified one).
-> [saved document names]

### `ignore_dependency_changes(doc, names=None)`

Clear the modified flag of the dependencies `names` of `doc` (None =
every modified one), so FreeCAD stops asking to save them; their changes
in memory are not saved (GUI only). -> [document names]

### `files_without_thumbnail(folder, recursive=True, size=256)`

FreeCAD files of `folder` whose stored thumbnail is missing or
narrower than `size` pixels (read from the files, nothing opened).
-> [paths]

### `generate_thumbnails(folder, recursive=True, only_missing=True, copy=True)`

Open, fit (isometric) and save the FreeCAD files of `folder` so that
each stores a 256 px thumbnail (GUI only: it is a capture of the view).
copy=True (default) works on a copy of the folder made next to it:
saving rewrites the files with this FreeCAD version. Files already open
are skipped. -> {"folder", "done", "skipped", "failed": [{"file",
"error"}]}
